canonical_question: Does the 'matrix inversion' of correlation functions become numerically unstable or ill-conditioned when the number of distinct pair clusters in a 5-component alloy exceeds the number of sampled configurations?

question_variants.question: Does the 'matrix inversion' of correlation functions become numerically unstable or ill-conditioned when the number of distinct pair clusters in a 5-component alloy exceeds the number of sampled configurations?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The evidence mentions the matrix inversion method for calculating probabilities but does not discuss numerical stability issues or the condition where distinct pair clusters exceed sampled configurations.

answers.answer: The text notes that probabilities are calculated via matrix inversion of correlation functions but does not address the numerical stability or ill-conditioning when the number of clusters exceeds sampled configurations.
answers.measurement_outcome: y n i j is calculated through a matrix inversion of correlation functions obtained via Canonical Monte Carlo (CMC) [70] .
answers.boundary_limitation: No discussion of numerical instability or configuration limits.
evidence_spans: The results here demonstrate that grain refinement only occurred when the heavy ions are introduced.
This suggests that such a grain refinement observed in the dual-beam irradiation case was caused by a cascade effect.
The in situ nature of the experiments performed in this work has allowed us to observe the grain refinement effect in real-time
